findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted as public with no ACL restriction, exposing customer master data (an .xlsx object containing customer data) to anyone on the internet.

The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects such as the customer master file are stored unencrypted, violating the requirement that encryption at rest be the default state.
No versioning block is configured, meaning objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, weakening data integrity protections.
A customer master file containing presumably sensitive customer data is uploaded to a bucket that is public and unencrypted, directly exposing confidential data.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial data unencrypted at rest despite the guidance that encryption should be the default state for stored data.
No versioning is enabled on the financials bucket, allowing accidental or malicious data loss with no recovery path.
No logging block is configured, so access to sensitive financial data cannot be audited.
The operations bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving stored data unencrypted.
No logging block is configured for the operations bucket, preventing audit trail of access to its contents.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored data (potentially sensitive datasets) is not encrypted at rest.
